name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean makes a Republican win extremely unlikely
Jasmine Clark has raised over $1.6 million with heavy outside support, while Jonathan Chavez reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%
Open seat after Everton Blair lost the full-term nomination, but the seat stays with the incumbent party
model.rationale: The district's D+21 baseline and the absence of any competitive signals point to a comfortable Democratic hold. Clark's strong fundraising and outside backing contrast with a Republican challenger showing no measurable campaign activity, and markets agree the race is effectively decided.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a credible Republican campaign or unexpected outside spending could narrow the margin, though the district's fundamentals leave little room for a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Atlanta-area House seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Georgia, with a partisan lean of D+21. David Scott's retirement set off a competitive Democratic primary, and Everton Blair lost the nomination for the full term, but the seat remains firmly in Democratic hands. Jasmine Clark enters the general election with a substantial financial advantage, having raised about $1.6 million and drawn more than $4 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez reports no fundraising on file.

No public general-election polling is available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 97%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The forecast expects Clark to win by a wide margin, with the main uncertainty being the size of the victory rather than the outcome.
